subject: MedSecure pilot — ingress corridor recommendation (peering vs endpoint vs encrypted tunnel)
messages:
From: Alex Morton <itops@medsecure.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shah <ciso@medsecure.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot connectivity needs and constraints

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this on — we start the MedSecure pilot next month and need a short recommendation on the connectivity pattern we should use to reach Redwood Private (VPC-hosted inference). High level constraints:

- PHI in transit (must be encrypted and auditable)
- Target p50 latency <= 30ms from our primary DC (us-west-2 region) to inference endpoints
- CIDR overlap with our existing cloud ranges (lots of /16s) — can’t renumber quickly
- Strict egress control — we only allow specific service IPs from production hosts
- Budget: pilot cost sensitivity, but we can justify one-time infra setup if it simplifies long term ops

We asked the vendor (Redwood) whether they support peering, endpoint services, and S2S VPN. Please outline tradeoffs and a recommended short-term (pilot) and medium-term (production) approach. If you have a checklist of what we need to gather from netops/security for each option, that would help.

Appreciate a concise decision memo.

-- Alex
Alex Morton
Head of Platform Ops, MedSecure
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morton <itops@medsecure.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <ciso@medsecure.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot connectivity needs and constraints

Alex — thanks, clear constraints. Attached is a short recommendation and an ingress diagram. Summary up front (TL;DR):

1) Pilot (recommended): configure an interface endpoint / hosted service (PrivateLink-style) for production tenant traffic plus a temporary site-to-site IPSec tunnel for dev/test and fallback.

2) Production (recommended long-term): prefer a dedicated interconnect (Direct Connect / Cloud Interconnect) if latency/stability demands hold, with PrivateLink in front of the inference service to minimize network surface and simplify firewall rules.

Why this split? PrivateLink-style endpoints restrict the attack surface (no route table pokes, ENI-based access), are easier to lock down with security groups and mTLS, and remove the need to change your global route tables (avoids CIDR collision issues). For the pilot, we can stand up an endpoint service in our VPC and grant MedSecure an interface endpoint from their VPC — that gets you encrypted traffic over the cloud fabric without public IPs.

Tradeoffs (short bullets):
- VPC peering: lowest operational complexity for intra-VPC north-south traffic, slightly lower latency than endpoint models in some clouds; but requires route table + ACL changes, fails with overlapping CIDRs, and increases blast radius (your VPC has network-level access into ours). Not ideal given your CIDR constraints and strict egress policies.
- Interface endpoint (PrivateLink): best for least-privilege production access, avoids CIDR renumbering, aligns well with PHI controls (we can require mTLS and enforce per-endpoint IAM/policies). Bandwidth and per-ENI throughput limits exist; we'll size ENIs/NLBs appropriately. Slightly higher operational cost vs peering but better security posture.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPSec): fastest to stand up, works around CIDR overlap (if you NAT) and on-prem->cloud, good for short-term. Latency/jitter is unpredictable over the internet; not recommended as the only path for latency-sensitive production workloads. Useful as a resilient fallback path during pilot.

Immediate checklist for us to collect from MedSecure (short):
- Your primary egress IP blocks and NAT topology
- VPC CIDR(s) and whether /16 renumbering is possible (yes/no)
- Preferred auth mode: mTLS certs, or IP/ACL + mutual TLS?
- Throughput baseline: concurrent sessions, average tokens/sec estimate (we'll size ENIs/NLBs)
- Contact + change window for your netops to add endpoint connection

I'll attach a 2-page decision memo, a diagram, and a sizing CSV. If you confirm the throughput numbers we can draft the endpoint service policy and the exact Security Group rules you'll need.

Next steps:
- If you want to proceed, we spin up a preview endpoint in our staging account and give you endpoint connection instructions + IAM policy.
- Optionally we can run a quick latency test from your DC to our staging endpoint.

Cc'ing Kim and Ben to validate operational/throughput assumptions.

Best,
So

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot connectivity needs and constraints

Quick ops notes (sizing / practical limits) — adding detail so MedSecure can make final call:

- Interface endpoints (AWS model) typically present per-ENI throughput constraints ~ 1-5 Gbps depending on flannel and cloud. For steady high-throughput inference we provision multiple endpoints behind an internal NLB (we manage sticky session mapping to preserve KV cache affinity). For your pilot numbers (see attached CSV) two interfaces should be fine.
- If you expect bursts of many concurrent short requests (chat-style), batching behavior matters. We'll recommend a short-lived warm pool so cold-call latency is bounded.
- Peering: routing complexity grows if MedSecure wants to reach multiple subnets in our VPC (we prefer not to expose internal control-plane subnets).
- VPN: if you want S2S as fallback, plan for a redundant pair of tunnels and BGP with max-prefix and monitoring. Don't rely on a single internet path for production.

Operational ask: please confirm whether your compliance team needs flow logs forwarded to your audit collector, or if it's sufficient to receive per-request audit records from Redwood's control plane (we can enable both).

If everyone agrees to the PrivateLink + S2S fallback approach for pilot, Soojin and I will prepare the endpoint-service template and the onboarding runbook.

-Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that lines up with our thinking. Priya (CISO) confirmed PrivateLink-first for pilot provided we can:

- enforce mTLS between our hosts and Redwood endpoints
- receive per-request audit headers (request id, timestamp, tenant id) for retention
- see an initial latency test to validate the <30ms P50 from our us-west-2 colo (we'll share an IP/agent)

Action items agreed:
1) MedSecure to share throughput numbers and NAT/egress details (Alex to send).
2) Redwood to produce endpoint-service policy, security-group snippet, and a staging latency test harness (Soojin + Ben).
3) If pilot latency is within the SLA, MedSecure will engage their procurement team to budget a Direct Connect line for production (timeline: Q2 planning).

I'll attach the netops contact sheet in a follow-up.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

-- Alex
